thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Page: High DNS resolver latency detected in eu-west-1a impacting inference paths, triggering elevated token latency and 5xxs for some customers

maria_oncall: seeing a spike in tail latencies and increased 502s from the hosted API. Rolling 15m p95 for text-generation up from 120ms -> 950ms.

jamie_sre: logs show a mix of long DNS lookup times and GRPC stream resets. e2e trace attached shows resolver RTTs hitting ~1.2s.

raj_network: confirmed resolver spoolback in az1a, likely internal resolver rate-limiting + upstream resolver jitter. My quick check: `dig +short @10.0.2.3 api.internal.redwood` sometimes times out, then returns 200ms-1s.

maria_oncall: tagging prod-traffic <-> routing team. Can we failover inference traffic away from az1a for high QPS model routes?

devon_platform: we have a routing policy that prefers az-local endpoints. I can patch policy to prefer cross-az endpoints for the affected model routes, but that will increase p95 by a small amount for some customers. Want me to flip it?

jamie_sre: recommend temporary: 1) switch routing policy for read-heavy routes to cross-az primary, 2) disable local resolver cache TTL bump for the controlplane, 3) increase kv-cache local TTL to avoid frequent controlplane lookups.

raj_network: enacted a short ACL to rate-limit the noisy resolver client that was generating ~40k qps from a faulty health-check loop. That brought qps down ~30%. Still seeing occasional 500ms+ resolves.

maria_oncall: devon, go ahead with routing change. jamie, can you run the runbook step for DNS cache regen? Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dns-cache-regen

devon_platform: applied routing change for routes: `model/large-gen`, `model/chat-v3`. Pushed config via `routingctl rollout --policy cross-az-priority --routes model/large-gen,model/chat-v3` — monitoring.

jamie_sre: running cache regen now: `kubectl -n controlplane rollout restart deployment/dns-cache` and watching kvcache warmup. Expecting transient 1-2min of higher controlplane calls.

ana_cs: heads-up to CS: we're seeing elevated errors for a subset of EU customers on hosted inference; mitigation in progress. I'll draft a short status note if impact persists >30m.

maria_oncall: after routing change p95 dropped to ~220ms and 502s rate down 85%. Some customers still seeing slow tails (edge cases).

raj_network: resolver upstream team flagged a misconfiguration causing high TTL churn on the authoritative side — they're rolling a fix to stabilize responses. ETA 12m.

jamie_sre: monitoring traces — KV cache hit rate improving after regen. No new 5xx from inference runtime.

devon_platform: rolling back the temporary ACL on the noisy client (it was a malformed health-check) — upstream fixed.

maria_oncall: marking as mitigated for now. Postmortem required since this touched routing + resolver config + a flaky health-check. Assigning follow-up to: oncall (maria_oncall), network (raj_network), platform (devon_platform).

ana_cs: I'll notify affected customers with a short summary: cause (resolver TTL churn + noisy client), mitigation (routing fallback + cache regen), and ETA for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Tags: network, dns, routing, oncall-handoff.

maria_oncall: leaving notes: need a guardrail to prevent health-check loops from generating 40k qps (rate-limiter + alert), and add automated fallback routing for route groups when resolver tail > 300ms for 2m.

jamie_sre: agreed. I'll own postmortem and add measurements for resolver tail to SLOs.

raj_network: will coordinate with upstream resolver team to add authoritative TTL sanity checks in deployment pipeline.

devon_platform: noted. Rolling a small change to make cross-az routing fallback automatic for high-latency resolver signals.

ana_cs: publishing customer note now. :white_check_mark:
